# Determine if String Halves Are Alike.

@example "Moon" has two o's and "LAKE" has an A and an E: two vowels on each side.
"MoonLAKE"
=> true

@example The left piece "pia" has two vowels, the right piece "nos" only one.
"pianos"
=> false

@example y is not a vowel, so "gyp" has none, while "sum" has one.
"gypsum"
=> false

# The shortest strings: both letters vowels, neither, or only one.
"Io"
=> true

"xz"
=> true

"ab"
=> false

# Capital vowels count: looking at lowercase only would see 0 against 2.
"AIxexo"
=> true

# Here lowercase only would see 0 against 0.
"UbOcdf"
=> false

# Y is a consonant: counting it would give 2 against 1.
"Yoga"
=> true

# No vowels in either piece, though both have a y.
"rhythm"
=> true

# Vowels on one side only.
"bcdfAE"
=> false

# Every occurrence counts: e twice matches an a and an i.
"eexaiz"
=> true

# o twice does not match o once.
"ooqoqq"
=> false

# The character at index n / 2 belongs to the right piece: 1 against 1 here,
# but 0 against 2 or 2 against 0 if the cut is one place off.
"ktaEvw"
=> true

# 0 against 2 here, but 1 against 1 if the cut is one place too late.
"bcdOuf"
=> false

# 1000 vowels: 500 in each piece.
""
=> true

# 500 vowels against 244: the counts differ by 256, so an 8-bit counter
# would find them equal.
""
=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"UkkUYbEO"
=> true

@gen 3 small
"Eo"
=> true

@gen 6 small
"yIYb"
=> false

@gen 9 small
"UIiy"
=> false

@gen 11 small
"UyoaiAZEei"
=> true

@gen 12 small
"ZkkyaUYYib"
=> false

@gen 14 small
"uZ"
=> false

# Full-size cases from gen.c: 1000 letters.
@gen 1
""
=> true

@gen 5
""
=> false
